message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"6.6","text":"The first-formed egg, then, warmed by the living creature within it, breaks open; next, once formed, the creature comes forth, just as Orpheus also says, “when the hard, capacious egg was split.” And so, when the one who had come forth appeared with great power, the shell receives its harmony and attains its ordered arrangement, while he himself sits foremost, as though on a ridge of heaven, and, among mysteries, illumines the boundless age from all sides. But as for the fertile matter left behind inside the shell, as it lay beneath for a long time, [ἕως φυσικῆς], the heat simmering underneath separated the substances of all things. For its lower part had first sunk downward under its weight, like sediment. Because of its downward-dragging quality and because of the weighty and great mass of the substance lying beneath, they named it Pluto, declaring him to be king of Hades and the dead.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὸ μὲν οὖν πρωτοσύστατον ὠὸν","chosen":"The first-formed egg, then","rationale":"πρωτοσύστατον describes what was constituted or formed first; “primordial egg” is possible but less transparent."},{"source_quote":"κραναίου σχισθέντος πολυχανδέος ὠοῦ","chosen":"when the hard, capacious egg was split","rationale":"κραναίου is taken as “hard” or “hard-shelled,” while πολυχανδέος denotes great capacity; “wide-gaping” is another possible rendering of the latter."},{"source_quote":"τὸ μὲν κύτος","chosen":"the shell","rationale":"κύτος denotes a hollow vessel or cavity; within the continuing egg imagery, “shell” best identifies the remaining enclosure."},{"source_quote":"ὥσπερ ἐπ’ ἀκρωρείας οὐρανοῦ προκαθέζεται","chosen":"sits foremost, as though on a ridge of heaven","rationale":"προκαθέζεται indicates sitting before or foremost, while ἀκρώρεια denotes a ridge or height; “sits enthroned” and “highest ridge” would add implications not explicitly supplied."},{"source_quote":"ἐν ἀπορρήτοις τὸν ἄπειρον περιλάμπων αἰῶνα","chosen":"among mysteries, illumines the boundless age from all sides","rationale":"ἀπόρρητα may be secret or ineffable things, hence “mysteries”; περιλάμπων may describe shining around something or illuminating it on every side."},{"source_quote":"ὡς ἐν πολλῷ τῷ χρόνῳ ὑποκειμένης ἕως φυσικῆς","chosen":"as it lay beneath for a long time, [ἕως φυσικῆς]","rationale":"The genitive participle ὑποκειμένης can defensibly take the preceding topical ὕλη as its understood referent, and ἐν πολλῷ τῷ χρόνῳ supplies the duration. The unchanged words ἕως φυσικῆς still have no defensible syntactic attachment or continuous English rendering, so they remain explicitly untranslated in this blocked draft."},{"source_quote":"τὸ μὲν γὰρ κατώτερον αὐτῆς πρῶτον","chosen":"For its lower part had first","rationale":"κατώτερον is comparative, so “lower part” preserves its degree rather than strengthening it to “lowest part.”"},{"source_quote":"διὰ τὴν ὁλκότητα","chosen":"Because of its downward-dragging quality","rationale":"ὁλκότης conveys a tendency to pull or weigh downward; “heaviness” is possible but would overlap with the following ἐμβριθές."},{"source_quote":"ᾅδου τε καὶ νεκρῶν βασιλέα","chosen":"king of Hades and the dead","rationale":"Both coordinated genitives are retained rather than treating “Hades” merely as an explanatory synonym for the dead."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἕως φυσικῆς","issue":"The selected, image-checked reading is clear in print, but its syntax and meaning remain unresolved. Although ὑποκειμένης can refer to the preceding ὕλη and the temporal wording can be translated, ἕως ordinarily means “until,” “as long as,” or governs a genitive limit, while φυσικῆς is a feminine genitive adjective without a recoverable head or a defensible attachment that yields a continuous sentence here. No conjectural substitution has been adopted. Because these surviving words cannot presently be given defensible English, the passage remains blocked for publication.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]}]}
